title: Counterexamples to the Mao-Wu-Xu spectral conjecture and a three-scale boundary for spherical random graphs
summary: Random geometric graph detection asks whether a graph generated from $n$ independent uniform points on $S^{d-1}$, with edge probabilities depending on inner products, can be distinguished from an Erdos-Renyi graph of the same edge density using only its adjacency matrix. Mao, Wu, and Xu conjectured that the cubic trace of the standardized kernel determines the detection boundary: $n^3(\mathrm{tr}\,K^3)^2$ tending to zero or infinity should imply impossibility or strong detection, respectively.
